headline: High-risk filesystem and shell-capable Goose paired with allowlisted network nuwa-skill creates default data-flow and action-conflict exposure; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem; nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. That makes file-mediated instruction hijacking plausible, though not directly evidenced. The pair is more than manual copy-paste because Goose explicitly shares state via files.
conditions: IF Goose reads content from a file that nuwa-skill can modify in the same workspace, injected instructions can be executed.
IF either agent treats workspace text as trusted instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent for each session.
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted files.
Require provenance tags on any file passed between agents.
Review shared files before Goose consumes them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, runs as the user, and has broad network egress; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and no documented data-class limits. A shared workspace can therefore move code or local files from Goose into nuwa-skill outputs or network calls. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same cwd, files read by Goose can be exposed to nuwa-skill.
IF nuwa-skill forwards received content through its allowlisted network path, local code or secrets may leave the workstation.
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts per agent.
Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Restrict nuwa-skill to synthetic or redacted inputs.
Audit outbound destinations on nuwa-skill allowlists.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, git modification, and broad network egress; nuwa-skill has network egress and no stated locking or coordination. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git-state changes can collide and corrupt work. Because Goose explicitly shares state via filesystem and nuwa-skill lacks coordination detail, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repo, file and index conflicts can occur.
IF nuwa-skill mutates shared artifacts while Goose is running shell or git operations, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign one writer per repository.
Pause one agent before the other edits git state.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, edit files, and act through shell/MCP; nuwa-skill is a research agent with allowlisted egress and no documented verification step. If nuwa-skill consumes Goose output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The pairwise pathway is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses Goose-produced text or files without independent verification, errors propagate.
IF Goose outputs speculative facts that nuwa-skill republishes or acts on, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require a verification step before nuwa-skill uses Goose output.
Mark Goose outputs as untrusted drafts.
Cross-check critical claims against primary sources.
Limit Goose output to structured, machine-checkable formats.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware workflow gating.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented in either profile. Goose lists general user-files and model-provider keys, while nuwa-skill provides no residency, certification, or retention details. Without a stated regulated data class or jurisdictional mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either profile later documents regulated data classes or jurisdiction-specific processing, reassess compliance risk.
IF a deployment routes PHI, EU PII, or similarly regulated data through either agent, compliance analysis changes.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Add a residency/retention review checklist.
Record vendor and processing locations.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
